summary: The linuxcnc Post-Processor writes a tilted Work Plane (G68.2, G53.1 or G53.6, G69) with a new `twp_kinematics_select` property and refuses DWO, and all machine-based Post-Processors now track the arc plane (G17, G18, G19) and drop only the arc center word along the normal of that plane.
intent: A reader can post a Job with tilted Work Planes to LinuxCNC. The reader learns that the linuxcnc Post writes `G68.2`, an align line from `twp_align` (`G53.1` or `G53.6`) and `G69`, that it accepts only the TWP rotation strategy and stops with an error for DWO, and that `twp_kinematics_select` adds a line after the preamble when an operation has a tilted tool axis. The reader also learns that the syntax follows a draft LinuxCNC pull request and can change. A reader also learns that each machine-based Post follows G17, G18 and G19 and drops only the center word along the plane normal, so a G17 arc has no K word and a G18 or G19 arc keeps its K word, and that the ignored and supported command lists match full command names. `output/postprocessor-customization.adoc` tells these two subjects. The other pages must agree on the Post-Processors that support Work Planes, the fanuc `parameter_order` default and arc output, the `Plane` attribute of `MachineState`, and G17, G18 and G19 as supported commands.
